text: Initial signaling to activate satellite cells following EIMD is purported to originate from muscle-derived nitric oxide, potentially in combination with the release of HGF (4, 269, 277). The process appears to be controlled at least to some extent by the cyclooxygenase (COX)-2 pathway, which is considered necessary for maximizing exercise-induced hypertrophic adaptations (257). COX-2 acts to promote the synthesis of prostaglandins believed to stimulate satellite cell proliferation, differentiation, and fusion (22). Research shows an enhanced myogenic response when inflammatory cells are abundant and a blunted response in their absence (22), suggesting that inflammatory processes subsequent to damaging exercise are critical to remodeling.
